subject: Post-call: first-emission (TTFT) targets, streaming transport & engineering handoff
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Verma <aisha@nexaanalytics.com>, Diego Alvarez <diego.alvarez@nexaanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: first-emission (TTFT) targets, streaming transport & engineering handoff

Thanks again for carving out time today — useful call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Summary of what we heard from Nexa (please correct if I missed anything):
- Primary UX requirement: users must see the first token (visual) quickly for scoring and live preview flows; target is a P99 time-to-first-token within the 100–200 ms range on your production traffic profile.
- Preferred streaming transport: you said WebSocket is preferred for multiplexed client sessions, but SSE is an acceptable fallback for simpler clients.
- Chunk cadence: you want small, frequent chunks to allow incremental UI rendering; initial guidance was ~30–80ms cadence or roughly 8–24 tokens per chunk for typical prompts.
- Throughput & concurrency: initial pilot target ~80 sustained RPS with bursts to 300 RPS; concurrent open streams per worker expected up to 150.

Our engineering ask / constraints:
- We need a short pilot data package (sample request traces + expected concurrency matrix) — I attached a CSV template.
- For Razor (our streaming runtime) to validate P99 TTFT in the 100–200 ms band, we'll need 2 weeks on a dedicated pilot lane (we propose 2 A100 GPUs / equivalent) and a small set of representative prompt shapes.
- Transport decision: if Nexa standardizes on WebSocket, we can provision a multiplexing config that reduces per-connection overhead; otherwise SSE path will require slightly different batching and heartbeat patterns.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Nexa to drop sample traffic and concurrency matrix into the attached nex a-sample-requests.csv by EOD Monday (2027-10-04).
2) Redwood to produce a short SLO proposal PDF with two configurations: WebSocket-first and SSE-fallback (attached).
3) Karthik to scope the engineering pilot and confirm resource needs (ETA: tomorrow).
4) Schedule a 30-minute pilot kickoff with Nexa engineering — propose Wed 2027-10-06 10:00 PT.

Questions for Nexa: can you confirm which client platforms will use streaming (web + iOS + Android?), and whether you have any hard upper bounds on P99 TTFT (e.g., must be <150ms)?

Attachments: nex a-sample-requests.csv (template), proposed-slos-ttft-pacing.pdf (draft), chunking-examples.txt

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0198

From: Aisha Verma <aisha@nexaanalytics.com>

Date: 2027-10-03T16:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: first-emission (TTFT) targets, streaming transport & engineering handoff

Logan — thanks for the clear notes. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Platform targets: web and iOS are in-scope for the first release; Android is planned for the following quarter.
- Hard SLO: our product team would like P99 TTFT <= 150 ms for the most common 2k-context prompts; if that's infeasible we'll discuss fallbacks.
- Transport: we prefer WebSocket because of session multiplexing; SSE only as a fallback for some embedded clients.
- Chunk cadence: we are flexible but aim for chunks that allow smooth typing preview — your 8–24 token guidance is reasonable.

We'll upload a 48-hour sample of production-like traffic and a short concurrency matrix to the spreadsheet by Monday morning.

One ask from our infra team: can Redwood surface a per-token cost estimate for the two pilot configurations (WS vs SSE) so we can include it in the pilot budget?

Aisha
Sr. Product Manager | Nexa Analytics

Logan / team — thanks, taking this on. Quick engineering readout and proposal for the pilot:

Engineering assumptions based on the ask: P99 TTFT <= 150 ms on 2k contexts, 80 sustained RPS with burst to 300 RPS, concurrent open streams up to 150.

Pilot proposal (high-level):
- Environment: isolated pilot cluster with 2 x A100 (or equivalent Ampere GPUs) + 64GB RAM per node.
- Model profile: we'll run the quantized 7B model first (q8_0 or q4 depending on quality) to hit TTFT targets. If quality is insufficient we'll test 13B quantized fallback.
- Runtime config: WebSocket-first routing with sticky sessions to reduce KV-cache cold starts; continuous batching window tuned to 10–30 ms for short prompts, with a fast-path for single-token priming to reduce first-token latency.
- Chunk strategy: emit ~12 tokens per chunk as default; dynamic chunk sizing allowed based on prompt shape. Aim for chunk cadence ~40–70 ms in steady-state.
- Telemetry: we'll instrument per-request TTFT, token-rate, batch-size distribution, and worker-level concurrency counters; link dashboards to you.

Validation plan: run a synthetic replay of your sample traffic (you upload CSV), measure P50/P95/P99 TTFT and steady-state throughput. If P99 > 150 ms we iterate batching/quantization/extra GPU.

Resource ask: please confirm NDA/contract terms so we can schedule dedicated pilot capacity; also drop the sample CSV by Monday as Logan requested.

I'll create a pilot runbook and share a calendar invite for the kickoff once we lock a time.

— Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
